common_name: Rijnveld's Golden Yellow Freesia (Classic Fragrant Yellow Freesia)

planting.note: Plant corms in fall in frost-free areas (zones 9-10) or start indoors 10-12 weeks before last frost in cold climates; a classic, long-established single-flowered yellow freesia cultivar.

directions: Plant corms 2 inches deep and 2-3 inches apart in gritty, well-drained soil; freesias resent wet conditions especially after bloom. Rijnveld's Golden Yellow bears fragrant, funnel-shaped, single flowers in a clear, bright golden yellow on arching, wiry stems, a long-established classic cultivar still commonly sold for its strong, sweet scent and reliable performance. Stems are slender and benefit from staking or a grow-through support to keep the flowers upright. In frost-free gardens the corms are perennial and naturalize freely; in colder climates lift after foliage dies, dry thoroughly, and store in a cool, dry place. Corms multiply quickly; divide every two to three years to maintain bloom quality.

Stems are slender and benefit from staking or a grow-through support to keep the flowers upright. common_name: Valerie Finnis Muscari (Pale Ice-Blue Grape Hyacinth)

planting.note: Plant bulbs 3-4 inches deep in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade in fall; Valerie Finnis is a pale-colored sport of the classic deep-blue Muscari armeniacum.

directions: Plant bulbs 3-4 inches deep in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade in fall. Valerie Finnis bears dense spikes of small, pale, silvery ice-blue flowers, a soft, unusual color sport of the classic deep-blue grape hyacinth named for the English plantswoman and photographer who discovered and popularized it. Its gentler color combines especially well with pale daffodils, white tulips, or other early-spring pastels where the more common deep-blue muscari might read as too bold. Like other grape hyacinths it naturalizes readily and multiplies into dense clumps over the years with no special care. Allow foliage to die back naturally after bloom, since it recharges the bulb for next year's flowers.

common_name: Golden Fragrance Muscari (Fragrant Bicolor Yellow Grape Hyacinth)

planting.note: Plant bulbs 3-4 inches deep in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade in fall; an unusual fragrant yellow-flowered grape hyacinth species selection, distinct from the common blue Muscari armeniacum.

directions: Plant bulbs 3-4 inches deep in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade in fall. Golden Fragrance bears dense spikes of small, tubular flowers opening deep purple-brown in bud and maturing to a bright golden yellow, with a strong, sweet banana-like fragrance unusual among grape hyacinths, most of which have little to no scent. Its warm coloring stands apart from the common blue and purple Muscari armeniacum cultivars that dominate the grape hyacinth market, offering a different color note for a mixed spring bulb planting. Like other grape hyacinths it naturalizes readily over the years with no special care. Allow foliage to die back naturally after bloom, since it recharges the bulb for next year's flowers.
